title: Understanding Generative Recommendation with Semantic IDs from a Model-scaling View

problem.claim: The work examines how generative recommendation models scale when using semantic IDs to combine item semantics with collaborative filtering signals.

gap.claim: Unlike generative models in other domains, SID-based generative recommendation has poorly understood scaling bottlenecks and quickly saturates as its components grow.

contributions.claim: The authors identify limited semantic-information capacity in semantic IDs as a fundamental bottleneck for SID-based generative recommendation.
The authors revisit Text-based Generative Recommendation as an alternative paradigm that directly represents items textually.
The authors analyze scaling behavior across model sizes from 44M to 14B parameters and position Text-based Generative Recommendation as a promising direction for foundation models.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments reportedly show that Text-based Generative Recommendation has superior scaling properties and achieves up to 20% improvement over the best achievable SID-based performance through scaling.
The authors report that LLMs' ability to model user–item interactions improves as the models scale, challenging the belief that LLMs struggle to capture collaborative filtering information.
Analyses across model sizes from 44M to 14B parameters reportedly underscore intrinsic scaling limits of SID-based Generative Recommendation.

narrative_sequence.summary: Generative Recommendation aims to unify item semantics and collaborative filtering signals, with semantic IDs used in one major paradigm.
SID-based Generative Recommendation exhibits rapid performance saturation as its modality encoder, tokenizer, and recommendation model are scaled.
Limited capacity of semantic IDs to encode item semantic information is identified as a fundamental bottleneck.
The work revisits Text-based Generative Recommendation as an alternative with potentially better scaling behavior.
The authors report improved scaling and up to 20% better performance for Text-based Generative Recommendation, alongside improved interaction modeling as LLMs scale.

source_observation.claim: Scaling separate components does not necessarily improve a system when an intermediate representation has limited information capacity.

interpretation.claim: Representation bottlenecks can dominate the scaling behavior of downstream generative systems.

application.claim: When scaling a modular recommendation system, evaluate the capacity and information loss of intermediate representations alongside model size.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this bottleneck generalizes beyond the studied semantic-ID recommendation setting.

source_observation.claim: Text-based representations reportedly scale better than semantic IDs, while larger LLMs improve user–item interaction modeling.

interpretation.claim: Retaining richer textual item information may support scaling both semantic and collaborative signals.

application.claim: Compare representation choices under matched scaling conditions rather than assuming compressed semantic codes are preferable.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify datasets, evaluation metrics, or experimental controls for the reported comparison.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, metrics, and statistical details are not provided.
The construction and capacity limits of the semantic IDs are not described.
The abstract does not provide per-component scaling results or experimental controls.
